title: What happens internally when System.exit() is called
answer: At a high level, `System.exit(status)` delegates to the runtime to begin JVM shutdown with the supplied status. The JVM enters its shutdown sequence, starts registered shutdown-hook threads in an unspecified order, waits for those hooks to finish, and then terminates the VM with the requested status unless shutdown is forcibly halted. Normal execution does not continue after the exit call. Cleanup that must happen during JVM shutdown should use appropriate lifecycle mechanisms such as shutdown hooks or framework/container shutdown callbacks rather than assuming ordinary code after `System.exit` will run.

steps.title: Inspect the call that starts JVM shutdown
steps.question: The next highlighted line invokes `System. exit(5)`, so control leaves ordinary application execution and the JVM begins its shutdown sequence. How does this call connect the status value supplied by application code with the registered hook that the runtime will execute before the Java process finally ends?
